$schema_note: Machine-readable derivative of docs/02-architecture/dependency-map.md. That document is the canonical, human-readable source; if this file and that document ever disagree, the document wins and this file is stale — regenerate it to match, per docs/00-overview/normative-precedence.md's rule for diagrams/derived artifacts. Do not hand-edit this file without also editing the source document in the same change.
edge_semantics: Each entry in 'depends_on' means the node depends on (requires) that dependency to function correctly, matching dependency-map.md's mermaid diagram direction exactly.

invariants.no_cycles: This graph must remain a DAG (docs/02-architecture/dependency-map.md's Circular-dependency rule). An AI agent adding a new edge must verify the addition does not create a cycle before committing — do not rely on manual inspection alone; run a topological sort and reject the change if it fails.
invariants.startup_order_is_a_topological_sort: docs/26-system-reference/02-startup-sequence.md's boot order must remain consistent with a valid topological sort of this graph — a new edge that would require reordering the startup sequence requires updating that document in the same change, per this file's atomic-update expectations (docs/26-system-reference/20-versioning-contracts.md's Atomic update checklist).
invariants.failure_domain_containment: A node's failure must only be able to affect its dependents (nodes with a path TO it via depends_on), never nodes outside that reachable set, per dependency-map.md's Failure-domain consequence section.

how_to_use_for_verification: Before adding a new service or a new dependency edge, add it to this file's 'edges' array (and the human-readable diagram in the same change, per the atomic-update rule).
Run a cycle-detection check (e.g., Kahn's algorithm / DFS-based topological sort) over the resulting graph.

If a cycle is detected, do not proceed — resolve it the way dependency-map.md's Circular-dependency rule describes (direction of data flow at a point in time, not mutual dependency), the same way the Verifier/State Manager near-cycle was resolved there.
